The figure below shows an ideal transformer with a turns ratio of $n$ between the primary and secondary coils. The primary coil is connected to a sinusoidal AC voltage source $u = U \sin \omega t$, while the secondary coil is connected to an AC ammeter and a motor. The motor has a coil resistance of $R$. When the motor lifts a mass $m$ at a constant speed, the ammeter reads a current $I$, and the acceleration due to gravity is $g$.

1. What is the current $I_0$ in the primary coil?
2. What is the electric power \( P \) of the motor?
3. What is the speed $v$ at which the heavy object is rising at a constant rate?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the left side is the primary coil of an ideal transformer, and the primary coil is connected only across the two terminals of a sinusoidal AC power supply labeled u; the right side is the secondary coil, and the secondary coil, AC ammeter A, and motor are connected in series to form a closed circuit. The right end of the motor lifts an object of mass m through a device, and the figure marks that the object moves upward at speed v. Reasoning: The reading I of the AC ammeter is the effective current in the secondary coil circuit. According to the problem statement and standard convention, the transformer turns ratio is n, and the ideal transformer current relation gives the effective current in the primary coil I0 = I/n. The peak value of the supply voltage u = U0 sin(omega t) is U0, so the effective voltage of the primary coil U1 = U0/sqrt(2). By the voltage ratio of an ideal transformer, the effective voltage of the secondary coil U2 = U0/(sqrt(2)n). The input electric power of the motor is P = U2 I = U0 I/(sqrt(2)n) = sqrt(2)U0 I/(2n). The motor coil resistance is R, and the Joule heat power is I^2 R, therefore the mechanical power used to lift the object is P - I^2 R. When rising at constant speed, the mechanical power equals mgv, so mgv = P - I^2R, solving gives v = [sqrt(2)U0 I/(2n) - I^2R]/(mg) = I(sqrt(2)U0 - 2nIR)/(2nmg).

The primary coil is connected to a sinusoidal AC voltage source $u = U \sin \omega t$, while the secondary coil is connected to an AC ammeter and a motor. The motor has a coil resistance of $R$. When the motor lifts a mass $m$ at a constant speed, the ammeter reads a current $I$, and the acceleration due to gravity is $g$.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the left coil of an ideal transformer is connected only to the sinusoidal source labeled u, and the right coil is connected in one series loop with the AC ammeter A and the electric motor; the motor lifts the mass m upward at speed v. Read from the text that the transformer turns ratio is n, the source voltage has peak amplitude U0, the ammeter reads secondary RMS current I, and the motor winding resistance is R. Use the ideal-transformer current relation matching the standard convention, so the primary RMS current is I0 = I/n. Convert the source peak voltage to RMS voltage: U1,rms = U0/√2, and use the voltage ratio to get the secondary RMS voltage U2,rms = U0/(√2 n). The motor electric input power is therefore P = U2,rms I = √2 U0 I/(2n). Since the motor winding dissipates Joule heat I^2R, the useful mechanical lifting power is P - I^2R. At constant speed, mechanical power equals mgv, so v = (P - I^2R)/(mg) = I(√2U0 - 2nIR)/(2nmg).

Finally, use ideal-transformer power/current matching to state the primary current I0 = I/n.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中左侧是交流电源，标有 u，接在理想变压器原线圈上；右侧副线圈接成一个单回路，回路中串联了交流电流表 A 和 electric motor。电动机右侧通过提升装置带动质量为 m 的重物，旁边标出重物以速度 v 向上运动。副边没有并联支路，所以副线圈、电流表和电动机中的电流相同。

推理：电流表读数 I 为交流有效值。原边电压 u = U0 sin(ωt)，所以原边电压有效值为 U0/√2。理想变压器匝数比为 n，按题设对应关系，副边有效电压为 Us = U0/(√2 n)。副边电流有效值为 I，因此理想变压器电流关系给出原边电流 I0 = I/n。

电动机的输入电功率为副边端电压有效值乘以电流有效值：P = Us I = U0 I/(√2 n) = √2 U0 I/(2n)。

电动机线圈电阻为 R，铜损功率为 I^2 R，因此转化为机械功率的部分为 Pmech = P - I^2 R。重物匀速上升，牵引力平衡重力，机械功率为 mgv。所以 mgv = √2 U0 I/(2n) - I^2 R。解得 v = I(√2 U0 - 2nIR)/(2nmg)。

raw_record.original_question:
The figure below shows an ideal transformer with a turns ratio of $n$ between the primary and secondary coils. The primary coil is connected to a sinusoidal AC voltage source $u = U \sin \omega t$, while the secondary coil is connected to an AC ammeter and a motor. The motor has a coil resistance of $R$. When the motor lifts a mass $m$ at a constant speed, the ammeter reads a current $I$, and the acceleration due to gravity is $g$.

1. What is the current $I_0$ in the primary coil?
2. What is the electric power \( P \) of the motor?
3. What is the speed $v$ at which the heavy object is rising at a constant rate?
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, the left side is the primary coil of an ideal transformer, and the primary coil is connected only across the two terminals of a sinusoidal AC power supply labeled u; the right side is the secondary coil, and the secondary coil, AC ammeter A, and motor are connected in series to form a closed circuit. The right end of the motor lifts an object of mass m through a device, and the figure marks that the object moves upward at speed v.

Reasoning: The reading I of the AC ammeter is the effective current in the secondary coil circuit. According to the problem statement and standard convention, the transformer turns ratio is n, and the ideal transformer current relation gives the effective current in the primary coil I0 = I/n. The peak value of the supply voltage u = U0 sin(omega t) is U0, so the effective voltage of the primary coil U1 = U0/sqrt(2). By the voltage ratio of an ideal transformer, the effective voltage of the secondary coil U2 = U0/(sqrt(2)n). The input electric power of the motor is P = U2 I = U0 I/(sqrt(2)n) = sqrt(2)U0 I/(2n). The motor coil resistance is R, and the Joule heat power is I^2 R, therefore the mechanical power used to lift the object is P - I^2 R. When rising at constant speed, the mechanical power equals mgv, so mgv = P - I^2R, solving gives v = [sqrt(2)U0 I/(2n) - I^2R]/(mg) = I(sqrt(2)U0 - 2nIR)/(2nmg).
